key_insight: Hydration-dependent diffusion drives water transport in anion exchange membranes, while swelling and mechanical feedback modify the transport response.
engineering_relevance: Coupled transport–mechanics modeling can inform membrane design for continuous CO2 separations under nonuniform hydration.
method: Transient finite element modeling of Fumasep FAA-3-50 with concentration-dependent water diffusivity.
Hygroscopic swelling and nonlinear viscoelasticity coupled to water transport.
Comparison of uncoupled, one-way coupled, and fully coupled formulations.
evidence_signal: The fully coupled model reproduces the hydration dependence of steady-state water-transport measurements, with strongest agreement at intermediate hydration levels.
watch_item: Validation reported in the abstract is steady-state; transient deformation predictions and performance at hydration extremes need further assessment.
paper_title: Modeling Transport and Mechanics in Anion Exchange Membranes to Optimize Continuous CO2 Separations
